title: Baptism
definition: Baptism is a public ordinance given by Christ that identifies a believer with His death, burial, and resurrection.
summary: Baptism publicly identifies believers with Jesus Christ and His saving work.
christFocus: Baptism points to union with Christ in His death and resurrection and publicly marks discipleship under His lordship.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Baptism is an ordinance commanded by Christ. It publicly identifies a person with Jesus and His people. It points to cleansing, union with Christ, death to the old life, and newness of life.

Baptism does not save by itself. Salvation is by grace through faith in Christ. Yet baptism is not meaningless; it is a serious and joyful act of obedience that visibly proclaims the Gospel.

Through baptism, believers confess that they belong to Christ and are joined to His people. It is a public sign of discipleship and a testimony to the saving work of Jesus.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people separate private belief from public obedience. Baptism matters because Jesus calls His disciples to openly identify with Him and His people.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: If you have trusted Christ and have not been baptized, prayerfully pursue obedience. If you have been baptized, remember what it signified: you belong to Christ and are called to walk in newness of life.
